title.value: The meaning of significant mean group differences for biomarker discovery
title.justification: The paper focuses on the interpretation of mean group differences in the context of biomarker discovery.
title.quote: Citation: Loth E, Ahmad J, Chatham C, López B, Carter B, Crawley D, et al. (2021) The meaning of significant mean group differences for biomarker discovery. PLoS Comput Biol 17(11): e1009477.

analysis.description: The paper discusses the challenges and considerations in interpreting mean group differences for biomarker discovery, particularly in psychiatric research involving heterogeneous conditions like autism. It emphasizes the limitations of mean group comparisons and the importance of effect size, sample size, and distribution shape in evaluating potential biomarkers.

type.justification: The paper uses simulations and theoretical exploration to discuss how statistical approaches can impact biomarker discovery.
type.quote: In this educational article, we used empirical data simulations to investigate how effect size, sample size, and the shape of distributions impact the interpretation of mean group differences for biomarker discovery.

name.justification: The paper is centered around the discovery and interpretation of biomarkers in the context of psychiatric conditions.
name.quote: Here, we used simulations to show that the latter statement is only true at very large effect sizes. We demonstrate that across different areas of autism research, mean group differences with small to large effects indicate that approximately 45% to 68% [cases] do not have an atypicality on cognitive tests or brain structure.

name.justification: The paper discusses neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions and their biomarkers.
name.quote: On the one hand, the clinical and etiological heterogeneity of most neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions (as well as substantial overlap between conditions) is widely accepted among researchers and clinicians.

name.justification: The paper frequently uses autism research as an example to illustrate its points on biomarker discovery.
name.quote: To exemplify this, we then applied these statistical criteria to evaluate the current state of biomarker discovery in one area of psychiatry where heterogeneity is well established—autism research.

name.justification: The paper mentions using data from the EU-AIMS LEAP cohort as part of its analysis.
name.quote: For instance, in the EU-AIMS LEAP cohort, we observed shifted developmental trajectories where the control group reached a ceiling effect in spatial working memory earlier than the autism group.

name.justification: The paper discusses the use of GWAS meta-analysis results in its evaluation of biomarker discovery.
name.quote: GWAS results from a recent meta-analysis yielded small effect sizes d = 0.06 with single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) passing corrected p-value for association.
